speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the character of your flank pain and tell me if you have noticed any fever, chills, or nausea. Also, have you seen any blood in your urine or noticed any changes in its color?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To further narrow down the cause, is this a one-time event or does it happen frequently, and have you noticed any fever, chills, or a burning sensation when urinating? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance: Reddish, WBC: 10-20 /HPF, RBC: Too numerous to count, Nitrites: Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Understood; I will focus on the most likely cause. Given your recurrent UTIs, flank pain, and visible hematuria, are you currently experiencing fever, chills, or nausea? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance: Reddish, WBC: 10-20 /HPF, RBC: Too numerous to count, Nitrites: Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive; Renal Ultrasound: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney.

The urinalysis confirms significant hematuria with sterile pyuria (negative nitrites), and the ultrasound findings of multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts are pathognomonic for Medullary Sponge Kidney. Your history of recurrent infections and flank pain is consistent with the stasis and stone formation often seen in this condition.
